headline: Taste-Bench measures long-horizon decision choices and reports gains from distillation
summary: The September 22 preprint introduces Taste-Bench, 502 decision-fork questions mined from software-engineering and AI-research agent trajectories. Models choose between two directions before seeing later outcomes; a question counts correct only when the choice is correct in both candidate orders, making chance accuracy 25%. The authors report GPT-5.6 Sol at 59.7% average accuracy, falling to 21.0% across models when decisive evidence appears only after substantial later work. On held-out engineering questions from unseen tasks, a distilled Qwen3.6-27B student scores 47.9% versus 30.0% for its base model. In a separate 41-task SWE-bench Pro experiment, a fixed executor succeeds on 14.6% with no advice and 33.7% with student advice; correct advice reaches 39.0%. These author-reported findings are not independent reproductions.
